components.name: Edge glow (sending, still)
components.description: Signature: the window edge carries the transfer's light. Shown here as the reduced-motion still ring.

narrative.overview:
A transfer is light passing from one window to the other. The window itself is the indicator: during a transfer its edge carries a blue comet out of the sender and fills the receiver with orange, ending in an arrival flash. Everything else stays quiet so that light reads: airy cool-white ground with a faint blue-to-orange wash settling into a rose-lilac horizon, a frosted white stage in a double bezel, ink-navy text, and soft mechanical keycaps sitting in a recessed tray.

Dark is the same world at night: a near-black canvas, deep-navy window ground with a blue horizon glow rising from the bottom edge, the same keys backlit more strongly, and the edge glow reading as real light. Density is calm desktop-utility: one window at 552px, one stage, a short header, a log that stays folded until asked for.

Each window is native to its OS (traffic lights and centred title on macOS, left title with app mark and caption buttons on Windows; window radius and action order follow the OS) while the brand inside is identical.
keyCharacteristics: Blue is the sending end, orange the receiving end; neutrals carry everything else.
The window edge is the progress indicator; the stage bar is the precise readout.
Buttons are softened keycaps with real travel, a skirt, a cast shadow and a backlight.
Wide-bold Mona Sans headings, normal-width body, Geist Mono only for machine output.
Frosted surfaces that go solid under reduced transparency; motion that becomes still light under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Two Ends Rule
rules.body: Blue means the sending end and orange means the receiving end, everywhere: keys, chips, tiles, glow, log lines. Never use either as decoration or as a generic "primary" colour. A screen with no transfer meaning should be almost entirely neutral.

rules.name: The Blend Is a Journey Rule
rules.body: The blue-to-orange gradient (via lilac) only appears where something travels from one end to the other: the progress fill, the edge-glow comet, the arrival flash, the brand mark's stroke, and the Paid pill's outline. It is never a background fill on a control.

rules.name: The One Outline Rule
rules.body: Among controls and tags, exactly one element carries the gradient outline: the Paid pill. The window edge glow is light that marks state and only shows during a transfer; it does not count toward this rule and is not an excuse for a second gradient-bordered control.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono appears only for what the machine produced or will execute: log lines, paths, commands. Never for labels, numbers in the UI or decoration; UI numbers use Mona Sans with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Wide Means Heading Rule
rules.body: The width axis goes above 104% only for the three heading roles. Body text always sits at 100%.

rules.name: The Docked Actions Rule
rules.body: A state's actions stay docked below its scrolling body; content scrolls, the action row does not. Only centred short states keep actions inline with their content.

rules.name: The Native Order Rule
rules.body: Action groups are right-aligned on both OSes, passed primary-first: macOS places the primary key rightmost, Windows places it leftmost. Never hard-code one order.

rules.name: The Light Is Not a Shadow Rule
rules.body: Coloured glow is light from a source: under a lit key, around a window during a transfer, inside the drop portal. Never use a coloured box-shadow as general elevation.

rules.name: The Glass Goes Solid Rule
rules.body: Under `prefers-reduced-transparency`, glass and shell surfaces become solid (white/#f1f3f7 light, navy-800/navy-850 dark) and blur is removed. Any new frosted surface must read from `--surface-glass`/`--glass-blur` so it inherits this.

rules.name: The Nested Radius Rule
rules.body: An inner surface's radius equals its container's radius minus the gap between them. Never put a larger radius inside a smaller one.

rules.name: The Settled Spring Rule
rules.body: Interface motion uses critically damped springs (bounce 0, about 0.42s) and `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` easing. Overshoot is reserved for physical travel: a key's release springs back (bounce 0.45) because a press carries momentum, and the sliding switch thumb settles with a barely perceptible layout spring (bounce 0.08). Nothing else overshoots.

rules.name: The Still Light Rule
rules.body: Under reduced motion every travelling or orbiting effect becomes a static state carrying the same information (still ring, breathing spinner, no live-dot pulse, stage states cross-fade without blur or rise); CSS transitions collapse to 1ms.

dos: **Do** change the look in `src/styles/tokens.css` and `src/styles/motion.ts`; components read semantic tokens only, including radii, tone rings and inset shadows. Add a token rather than a literal value in a module.
**Do** use blue for anything about the sending end and orange for anything about the receiving end, including log lines, chips and tile icons.
**Do** build every new button as a Key (plain, ink or lit) and give each action group at most one ink key.
**Do** order actions primary-first and let the OS decide which side the primary sits on; dock them below the scrolling pane body.
**Do** nest radii as container minus gap (stage 28px, plate 22px).
**Do** draw edges with 1px hairline rings and a top highlight instead of borders.
**Do** keep every frosted surface on `--surface-glass` and `--glass-blur` so it goes solid under reduced transparency.
**Do** give every travelling or orbiting effect a still equivalent under reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** use blue or orange as decoration, or as a generic brand fill on a neutral control.
**Don't** add a second gradient-outlined control or tag; the Paid pill is the one.
**Don't** set UI labels, numbers or headings in Geist Mono; it is for logs, paths and commands only.
**Don't** use the width axis above 104% for body text.
**Don't** add overshoot beyond a key's release and the switch thumb's slight layout spring.
**Don't** use Apple or Windows logos, or any brand elements from reference material; the brand mark is the only identity asset.
**Don't** put a larger radius inside a smaller one, or make the stage anything other than the largest in-app radius.
